com_001: You can recognise it by its trunk, about 8.2 metres round, the thickest in Como's list, ringed by protective stakes and a bark wrap. It stands in the Parco di Villa Olmo.
com_002: You can recognise it as the larger of a pair of drooping cedars closing the end of the promenade, over a lakeside fountain. It stands at Villa Geno, Viale Geno.
com_003: You can recognise it by its height, 33 metres, the tallest on the lakefront walk, its bark shedding in plates to leave a mottled cream and olive trunk. It stands at Villa Geno.
com_005: You can recognise it by its flat, tiered crown, readable layer above layer, standing directly in front of the house. It stands in the grounds of Villa del Grumello.
com_006: You can recognise it by standing beside the old greenhouses, its whole crown turning gold and dropping within days each November. It stands in the grounds of Villa del Grumello.
com_007: You can recognise it by its dark, glossy evergreen leaves and huge scented white flowers in May and June, visible from across the lawn. It stands at Villa del Grumello.
com_009: You can recognise it in May by its crown going up in white flower candles, beside the tenth-century church of Santi Filippo e Giacomo. It stands in Quarcino.
